text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad launched the National Information Technology Agenda on Thursday which is set to make the country a centre of excellence for multimedia technology.
-- Participants in Malaysia's ambitious Multimedia Super Corridoor project were announced by Mahathir on Thursday. They involve 29 major foreign and local information technology-related companies.
-- Malaysians will be able to use their television sets to access the Internet using a set-top box by September 1997, said Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts, Leo Moggie.

-- Total investible funds, including unit trusts, insurance and pension funds, are expected to rise to 440 billion ringgit by 2000, from the current 230 billion ringgit, said Deputy Finance Minister Wong See Wah on Thursday.

-- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) needs to see a higher proportion of instituitional investors so that price movements can be governed by fundamentals, said KLSE executive chairman Nik Mohamed Din Nik Yusoff on Thursday.
